title: Setting, candidate table, Lean structure, and open math for the A≥3 binding extension
html:
Setting — the A \ge 3 binding gap

The binding-endomorphism analogy closes the deuteron via B = m_e \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) \cdot \Delta\mathrm{tr} to +0.19 %, but undershoots A \ge 3 by 44–72 %. Diagnosis: \Delta\mathrm{tr} is the linear truncation of \log(\mathrm{tr}) \sim \mathrm{Vol}; the extensive observable lives in the per-rep q-Reeb rotation phase on the column-rich irrep of a substrate-fixed force-carrier torus knot.

The α_shift universal chain proves \alpha_{\text{shift}}(T_{p, k}) = k \cdot (p - 1) — the pole order of σ on the column-rich irrep, equivalently the boundary holonomy of the Yekutieli non-abelian Stokes integral around the column cycle. This is the same boundary holonomy that the per-rep q-Reeb rotation phase records.

The unification

Per nucleus A, identify the substrate-specific force-carrier torus knot T(p_A, k_A) whose α_shift sets the per-rep Reeb eigenvalue. The binding closure is then

  B(A) = m_e \cdot \rho_0 \cdot \alpha_{\text{shift}}(T(p_A, k_A))
       = m_e \cdot \rho_0 \cdot k_A \cdot (p_A - 1).
nucleus A hypothesised T(p, k) α_shift status
deuteron (D) 2 T(2, 3) candidate 3 open
tritium (T) 3 T(2, 5) candidate 5 open
^3He 3 T(2, 5) candidate (mirror) 5 open
^4He 4 T(3, 4) candidate 8 open

The candidate (p, k) values are hypothesised; the rigorous identification from the substrate's Hecke-Wedderburn block structure on H_{3A}(q) is open.

The deuteron candidate T(2, 3) is motivated by the following rationale:

  1. Smallest non-trivial torus knot. T(2, 3) is the trefoil — the minimum-pole-order column-rich irrep, matching the deuteron's role as the lightest A \ge 2 nucleus.
  2. \mathcal{B}_3-braid-closure consistency. The binding-endomorphism analogy closes the deuteron via B = m_e \cdot \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) \cdot \Delta\mathrm{tr} to +0.19\,\%. T(2, 3) is the canonical boundary torus knot of \mathcal{B}_3 (the trefoil is the (2, 3)-cable of the core circle in \mathcal{B}_3's Seifert fibre structure).
  3. Calibration consistency. Per binding-rotation-phase-lead.witness.json, the deuteron's full Markov-weighted q-Reeb phase aggregation gives \rho_{\mathrm{full}}(D) = 14.6673 MeV/rad. With \alpha_{\mathrm{shift}} = 3 and m_e \approx 0.511 MeV, the abstract substrate coupling \rho_0 in the class signature reads \rho_0 = B(D) / (m_e \cdot 3) \approx 1.451 — a dimensionless ratio (its \mathrm{rad}^{-1} unit arises only when the result is re-multiplied by the 14.6673 MeV/rad phase-scale measurement to recover B(D)). Note that \rho_0 (the class field) and \rho_{\mathrm{full}}(D) (the witness output) are distinct quantities — one is the substrate-universal coupling, the other the per-deuteron phase-weighted aggregation — bridged by the \alpha_{\mathrm{shift}} = 3 normalisation.

This is the A\ge3 analogue of:

  • meson-color-tube-uniqueness for m_K / m_\pi (smallest non-trivial pair \{T(2, 3), T(2, 4)\});
  • em-coupling-bring-zero-mode for 1/\alpha_{\rm EM} (genus-4 Bring pair \{T(2, 9), T(3, 5)\});
  • the T(2, k) tower for lepton + electroweak masses (W k=4, Z k=6, τ k=7, H k=8).

Lean structure

  • class BindingPerRepReebPhase B m_e ρ_0 — substrate axiom: per-rep Reeb phase factorisation, with field αShiftAt : ℕ → ℕ recording the per-A pole order and factors axiomatising B(A) = m_e \cdot \rho_0 \cdot \alpha_{\text{shift}}(A).
  • class BindingForceCarrierKnot αShiftAt p k — substrate axiom: the per-A pole order \alpha_{\text{shift}}(A) is realised by the proved formula k(A) \cdot (p(A) - 1) at a substrate-identified torus knot.
  • theorem binding_unique_via_alpha_shift — sorry-free conditional on the two classes: two binding evaluators sharing (m_e, \rho_0, \alpha_{\text{shift}}) agree pointwise.
  • theorem binding_subsingleton — Subsingleton companion.

Concrete light-nuclei candidate instance

The candidate table above is realised as a single Lean instance covering all four light nuclei A \in \{2, 3, 4\}:

  • def lightNucleusP, def lightNucleusK — case-split selectors over A \in \{2, 3, 4\} with sentinel 0 elsewhere. The three branches encode D \mapsto T(2, 3), T / {}^{3}\mathrm{He} \mapsto T(2, 5), {}^{4}\mathrm{He} \mapsto T(3, 4).
  • def lightNucleusAlphaShift A := bindingAlphaShift (lightNucleusP A) (lightNucleusK A) — defined directly as the structural composition, so all downstream proofs close definitionally.
  • theorem light_nucleus_alpha_shift_at_deuteron|A3|He4 — per-branch sanity checks, each closing by a single rfl (deuteron: \alpha_{\mathrm{shift}} = 3; A=3 mirror: \alpha_{\mathrm{shift}} = 5; ^4He: \alpha_{\mathrm{shift}} = 8).
  • instance lightNucleiForceCarrierKnot : BindingForceCarrierKnot lightNucleusAlphaShift lightNucleusP lightNucleusK — discharges matches_alpha_shift definitionally; the instance body is matches_alpha_shift _ := rfl. No sorry.

All four nuclei are carried by this single instance rather than by four per-nucleus instances, so the identification pattern is stated once and the full candidate table is discharged in one place.

Remaining open math

What is open is to identify the specific (p_A, k_A) for each light nucleus A. The candidate hypotheses in the table above are informed by:

  • the deuteron's \rho_0 \approx 14.7 MeV/rad calibration from the formal derivation;
  • the mirror pair (T/^3He) \rho \approx 18.5 MeV/rad — ~25 % rise from the deuteron, suggesting a per-λ jump in pole order;
  • the q-Hamiltonian rotational-scale canonical evaluation (the formal derivation) confirms \mu_0 \approx 1.63 MeV is derived from the universal-ilp construction, narrowing the open question to the per-A force-carrier knot choice, not the scale.

Closing it — proving why specifically T(2, 5) carries A=3 mirror binding etc. — requires the per-nucleus minimisation argument on H_{3A}(q)'s Wedderburn block at the binding's smallest non-trivial irrep. Lean target: a theorem deriving (p_A, k_A) from a Hecke- trace minimisation principle, analogous to the still-open meson force-carrier derivation at prop:meson-color-tube-uniqueness.
